channel.title: Peninsula Insider
channel.description: Editorial coverage of the Mornington Peninsula - eat, stay, do, wine, and the weekend curated.

item.title: Insider Picks: 1 September 2026
item.description: Wood-fired lamb under the olive grove at Green Olive in Red Hill, the first wattle flush on the Bushrangers Bay Track, and the Hill & Ridge Market back from its winter break.

item.title: The Last Weekend of Winter
item.description: Winter's last weekend goes to the Sunday roast at The Epicurean in Red Hill South, the Bushrangers Bay Track at Cape Schanck while the southerly swell is still running, and Pt. Leo Estate's sculpture park, free for Peninsula locals on weekdays until 31 August.

item.title: Boat Moorings and Berths on the Mornington Peninsula
item.description: Annual mooring waiting lists, seasonal moorings you can actually book this season, and the one short-stay berth at Mornington Pier itself - the honest picture of where to put a boat on the Peninsula, and who to actually contact.

item.title: Insider Picks - 17 August 2026
item.description: Sunday lunch at Ten Minutes by Tractor, the Arthurs Seat Eagle open for morning rides in clear winter light, and a closing-weekend chance to see ceramics from Tuck Studio at MPRG.

item.title: The Winter Long Lunch: Vineyard Dining Room or Coastal Pub
item.description: Two very different versions of the same afternoon. Here's how to pick the right one for the day you're actually having.

item.title: Insider Picks - 12 August 2026
item.description: Moke Dining's five-course winter set menu in Flinders, the gannet colony at Point Danger in peak winter season, and the Helen Britton retrospective closing at MPRG this Sunday.

item.title: Insider Picks: 10 August 2026
item.description: The Bay Hotel Mornington's vault dining room for a winter occasion, the Red Hill Brewery Secret Stash Weekend this Saturday and Sunday, and the Balnarring Pub for a counter meal beside an open fire.

item.title: Stonier Fire & Wine Lunch, a Winter Whale Watch Window, and Buckwheat Galettes in Mornington
item.description: Stonier Wines fires up a winter lunch in Merricks, the whale migration corridor off Cape Schanck peaks in August, and Ouest France Bistro's buckwheat galette with ham and gruyère earns a Saturday morning detour.

item.title: Indoor Play on the Mornington Peninsula: The Four Worth Driving To
item.description: When the weather turns and the kids need to run, there are four indoor play venues on the Peninsula that actually hold up. Here is what each one is good for, and the five things to check before you leave the house.

item.title: Insider Picks: 6 August 2026
item.description: A Thursday market in Hastings, Friday aperitivo at Trofeo Estate, and two final winter weeks at Mornington Peninsula Regional Gallery.

item.title: Insider Picks: 2 August 2026
item.description: Mr Vincenzo's parmesan-wheel gnocchi on Mornington's main street, a winter walk along the dramatically emptied Flinders cliff path, and live country music at Tar Barrel today.

item.title: Insider Picks - 1 August 2026
item.description: St Andrews Beach Brewery's Sunday roast in the old stables, a winter low-tide walk at Bushrangers Bay, and Two Bays Brewing's gluten-free pale ale that non-coeliacs keep quietly ordering.

item.title: Insider Picks: 31 July 2026
item.description: The Sorrento Hotel's parma on Ocean Beach Road, the winter-emptied Gunnamatta back-beach trail, and a community sleepout at The Ranch in Boneo this Friday night.

item.title: Insider Picks - 30 July 2026
item.description: A morning bun at Sourdough Kitchen in Mornington, the winter surf at Gunnamatta, and Pt. Leo Estate's free sculpture park for locals through August.

item.title: Avani Syrah, Elgee Park's 1972 Vines, and Country Day at Tar Barrel
item.description: Avani's biodynamic Syrah at Red Hill, a walk through the Peninsula's oldest vineyard at Elgee Park, and a Sunday afternoon of live country music and local wine at Tar Barrel in Mornington.

item.title: Doot Doot Doot in winter, the Southern Peninsula Sleepout, and two shows closing at MPRG
item.description: A full degustation under 10,000 hand-blown glass orbs at Doot Doot Doot, a community sleepout at Boneo's Ranch, and Helen Britton's jewellery survey at Mornington Peninsula Regional Gallery before it closes 23 August.

item.title: Insider Picks: 27 July 2026
item.description: The rotating taps at Jetty Road, the Farnsworth Track's cliff-view shortcut, and a hot chocolate in Flinders that justifies the drive.

item.title: Insider Picks: 25 July 2026
item.description: Get to Flinders Sourdough before the miche goes, walk the Coppins Track clifftops to Diamond Bay, and buy your vegetables where the restaurants buy theirs.

item.title: Insider Picks: 24 July 2026
item.description: A fireside duck dish at Ten Minutes by Tractor, a winter dawn walk to Cape Schanck, and a photography show closing soon at Mornington's two-storey gallery.

item.title: Peninsula This Weekend - 18 to 19 July
item.description: July sits in the quieter stretch of Peninsula winter, and that is the point. The lead booking is a truffle hunt at Red Hill. Sunday is for the sculpture park at Pt. Leo.

item.title: Winter indoors: MPRG's winter program and the rainy day circuit
item.description: Four exhibitions and a children's space at Mornington Peninsula Regional Gallery until 23 August, and how to build a full wet day around them.

item.title: Peninsula This Weekend - 11 to 12 July
item.description: A proper wet winter weekend concentrates everything. The answer on a day like this is one indoor booking with some real weight to it - truffle country, a long lunch, or the pools when the air outside is genuinely cold.

item.title: Insider Picks - 5 July: The Winter Edit
item.description: Quealy Winemakers's winter kitchen, the Cape Schanck boardwalk at its most dramatic, and MPRG's current show before it closes.

item.title: Peninsula This Weekend - 4 to 5 July
item.description: The first full school-holiday weekend of winter is simple: one booked truffle hunt, one Sunday heritage train run, and one indoor family plan that does not feel like a fallback.

item.title: Peninsula This Weekend - 27 to 28 June
item.description: The solstice crowd has gone home. This is the quiet winter weekend of truffle hunts, local markets, and the final Sunday Sessions at the springs.

item.title: Peninsula This Weekend - 20 to 21 June
item.description: The solstice weekend moves from Sorrento's festival foreshore on Saturday to the stillness of the springs and the forest on Sunday.

item.title: The Sorrento Solstice Festival: A Night When the Peninsula Burns
item.description: The longest night of the year deserves a proper send-off. Two days on the Sorrento foreshore, a six-metre effigy on the bay, and the particular magic of a winter festival done right.

item.title: Peninsula This Weekend - 13 to 14 June
item.description: The week after King's Birthday: truffle season at its most available, cellar doors open and unhurried, and the Peninsula genuinely itself again.

item.title: Peninsula Notes - June 2026
item.description: Truffle season begins on the ridge. The fog is back most mornings. Flinders is doing something unusual for a coastal town in winter: it is full.

item.title: The One Booking Peninsula Day
item.description: Most Peninsula days are over-planned. The ones that work usually aren't. One table, one walk, one decision made in the morning about which direction the rest of the day will go.

item.title: Why the Peninsula Works Better in Winter
item.description: Empty dining rooms, cheaper rooms, and the particular quality of light that makes the ridge look like a different country. The case for coming in July rather than January.

item.title: Peninsula This Weekend - 6 to 7 June
item.description: King's Birthday is the loudest winter weekend on the Peninsula. Two clear moves, and the rest of the weekend kept open.

item.title: Peninsula This Weekend - 30 to 31 May
item.description: Autumn closes and winter opens on the same patch of Main Ridge on Saturday: the Peninsula marking its own calendar.

item.title: Peninsula This Weekend - 23 to 24 May
item.description: The Saturday markets are dark and truffle season is a week away: what's left is the Peninsula in its most deliberate register.

item.title: Peninsula This Weekend - 16 to 17 May
item.description: Mid-May gives the Peninsula back to itself. One forest morning, one market Sunday, nothing that needs to be organised beyond that.

item.title: Peninsula This Weekend - 9 to 10 May
item.description: Mother's Day is the organising principle. Book lunch first, then let the rest of the weekend behave.

item.title: Dromana: The Peninsula Insider Guide
item.description: Dromana is the Peninsula's practical gateway - a bay town at the foot of Arthurs Seat with easier edges than the famous villages further south. Come when you want a base that can do beach, ridge and family logistics without pretending to be something rarer than it is.

item.title: Flinders: The Peninsula Insider Guide
item.description: Flinders is the quiet southern village that proves the Peninsula does not need theatre to be good. Come for the harder light, the ocean edge, and a day shaped by a walk, a bakery and one proper lunch rather than a schedule full of noise.

item.title: Main Ridge: The Peninsula Insider Guide
item.description: Main Ridge is the Peninsula's highest, coolest and most wine-serious pocket - less a village than a plateau of good decisions. Come when you want the Peninsula stripped back to vineyards, fog, lunch and roads lined with trees rather than distractions.

item.title: Merricks: The Peninsula Insider Guide
item.description: Merricks is the understated corridor between bay and ridge where the Peninsula's wine country starts to feel private. Come for the general store, the estates, the pub and the rare pleasure of a district that seems to know exactly how little fuss it needs.
